claims.text: Compositional complexity-induced lattice distortions drive enhanced high-temperature mechanical behavior in refractory HEAs.
Compositional complexity-induced lattice distortions drive modified high-temperature thermoelastic behavior in refractory HEAs.
Lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Lattice distortions promote increased dislocation storage.
Increased dislocation storage produces more pronounced strain hardening.

Refractory HEAs and conventional refractory-alloy controls can be compared under identical high-temperature thermomechanical loading using mechanical testing, in situ neutron diffraction, and dislocation-density analysis.
Persistent lattice distortion and evolving dislocation density mediate strain hardening.
Persistent lattice distortion and evolving dislocation density mediate thermoelastic recovery.
Under high-temperature mechanical loading, hindered dislocation motion causes a buildup of dislocations.
The proposed mechanism will appear as sustained lattice strain in in situ neutron-diffraction measurements.
Post-deformation dislocation analysis can confirm the proposed dislocation buildup.
At high temperature, refractory HEAs will exhibit higher residual lattice strain than conventional refractory alloys.
At high temperature, refractory HEAs will exhibit a delayed reduction in thermoelastic recovery relative to conventional refractory alloys.
During high-temperature deformation, refractory HEAs will show a greater increase in dislocation density than conventional refractory alloys.
Conventional refractory alloys will have lower lattice distortion than refractory HEAs under the same high-temperature conditions.
Conventional refractory alloys will store fewer dislocations and consequently exhibit less strain hardening than refractory HEAs.
The proposed mechanism is significant at high-temperature service conditions.
The proposed effects may be less pronounced at lower temperatures because thermal activation is insufficient to amplify lattice-distortion effects and dislocation interactions.
Grain boundaries and secondary phases may contribute to the measured behavior in addition to compositional complexity and lattice distortion.
A lack of greater persistent lattice distortion or dislocation storage in the HEA, or a lack of correlation between dislocation dynamics and the target behaviors, would falsify the hypothesis.
